liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Good Lovin'** (2 reviews, 1 other source): Reviewer calls this version fun and primitive; Reviewer says the set becomes more structured after this song, which was itself somewhat experimental [2][6][12]
- **Me & My Uncle** (2 reviews): Reviewer finds the jams in this song unusual compared with other 1969 performances; Reviewer describes a long, jammy version of this song [3][4]
- **Instrumental** (1 review): Reviewer thinks it resembles a very slow Rocky Raccoon, perhaps the band noodling during equipment problems [10]
- **Smokestack Lightning** (1 other source): Only the final verses of the song are present on this recording [2]
- **Dark Star** (1 review): Reviewer notes a rare daytime Dark Star, with Garcia's classic SG tone and the original arrangement intact [11]

## Setlist highlights

- **Instrumental**: earliest performance in the archive; rare: 3 archived performances [15]
- **Good Lovin'**: back after 124 archived shows (1084 days) [15]

## The recordings

- **gd1969-05-07.sbd.des.5179.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 10 songs; 100 min; rated 3.4/5 by 5 [1]
- **gd69-05-07.sbd.cotsman.6028.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 8 songs; 93 min; rated 3.69/5 by 16 [2]. Said about its sound: Sound is less sharp than other shows of the era but decent; reviewer grades it about A; Sound is decent for its year and gear, but needs EQ adjustment for playback [4][11]

## Around the show

- Free concert in May 1969; reviewer notes Garcia played pedal steel, acoustic and electric guitar [7]
- Reviewer recalls KMPX radio announcing that morning that the Airplane and the Dead would play free that afternoon at the Polo Fields [9]
- Uploader marks forty years since the free concert in the park [11]
- Reviewer considers this show underrated and says the band plays very tightly [5]
- Reviewer says the band's sound was turning more down-home in this period, with heavy, crazy jams [7]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1969-05-07.sbd.des.5179.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by DES; source: SBD > MR > C > DAT > CD [1]
- **gd69-05-07.sbd.cotsman.6028.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Ernie Presley and J. Cotsman; source: Soundboard [2]
